Cause: The OSPF hello intervals don't match on the r2–r3 link, so no adjacency forms and r1 never learns 3.3.3.3/32. r2's eth2 is set to a 5-second hello interval, and r3's eth1 uses the 10-second default.

Evidence:
- r1's routing table has no 3.3.3.3/32. It has 10.0.0.4/30 and 2.2.2.2/32, both learned from r2.
- r2's only OSPF neighbor is 1.1.1.1. r3's OSPF neighbor list is empty.
- r2's running config for `interface eth2` (to-r3) has `ip ospf hello-interval 5`.
- r3's running config for `interface eth1` (to-r2) has no hello-interval setting, so it uses the default of 10 seconds.
- OSPF neighbors only form when hello intervals match. Both sides are point-to-point and in area 0, so the hello interval is the only difference in the configs.
- `ping 10.0.0.6` from r2 succeeds, so the link works at layer 3 and the fault is in OSPF.

Suggested fix: Make the hello intervals match on the r2–r3 link. Either remove `ip ospf hello-interval 5` from r2 eth2 so it uses the default of 10, or set `ip ospf hello-interval 5` on r3 eth1. Setting it on r3 also moves r3's dead interval to 20 seconds, so match that on r2 if it isn't already. After that, the adjacency should reach Full and r1 should learn 3.3.3.3/32.
